I'll help you set up a git server with automatic deployment to a web server. Here's the complete setup:

## Server Setup (on your server machine)

### 1. Create a bare git repository

```bash
mkdir -p /git/server
cd /git/server
git init --bare
```

### 2. Create the deployment directory

```bash
mkdir -p /var/www/html
```

### 3. Set up the git post-receive hook

Create `/git/server/hooks/post-receive` with the following content:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
GIT_WORK_TREE=/var/www/html git checkout -f
```

Make it executable:
```bash
chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive
```

### 4. Start a web server on port 8080

Use a simple Python HTTP server or Node.js. Here's Python:

```bash
cd /var/www/html
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

Or if you prefer something persistent, install and run nginx or Apache. For a quick test, you can also use:

```bash
cd /var/www/html
npx http-server -p 8080
```

## Client Usage (on your local machine)

Once SSH login is configured, you can then:

```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server myrepo
cd myrepo
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

Then verify:
```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
```

## How it works

- The bare git repository (`/git/server`) receives pushes
- The `post-receive` hook automatically checks out the latest code to `/var/www/html`
- The web server serves files from `/var/www/html` on port 8080

That's it! The post-receive hook makes deployment automatic—every push deploys instantly.

I'll help you set up a git server with automatic deployment to a web server. Here's the complete setup:

## Server Setup (on your server machine)

### 1. Create a bare git repository

```bash
mkdir -p /git/server
cd /git/server
git init --bare
```

### 2. Create the deployment directory

```bash
mkdir -p /var/www/html
```

### 3. Set up the git post-receive hook

Create `/git/server/hooks/post-receive` with the following content:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
GIT_WORK_TREE=/var/www/html git checkout -f
```

Make it executable:
```bash
chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive
```

### 4. Start a web server on port 8080

Use a simple Python HTTP server or Node.js. Here's Python:

```bash
cd /var/www/html
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

Or if you prefer something persistent, install and run nginx or Apache. For a quick test, you can also use:

```bash
cd /var/www/html
npx http-server -p 8080
```

## Client Usage (on your local machine)

Once SSH login is configured, you can then:

```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server myrepo
cd myrepo
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

Then verify:
```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
```

## How it works

- The bare git repository (`/git/server`) receives pushes
- The `post-receive` hook automatically checks out the latest code to `/var/www/html`
- The web server serves files from `/var/www/html` on port 8080

That's it! The post-receive hook makes deployment automatic—every push deploys instantly.
